summary: Fusing the sub / remainder / expert_map-gather launches into one Triton kernel is a real, exactly-attributable launch-count reduction on the launch-bound T<=8 shapes (decode_1 runs ~43 kernels in 172 us, nearly serial), nothing landed interacts with it, and no companion run would make a flat result more interpretable; proceed, with the implementation cautions on signed modulo and Triton specialization/compile timing below.
justification: A. Mechanism: master (sglang-pipeline-parity) computes local_ids = (topk_ids - data['local_start']) % N_EXPERTS in kernel_fn (submission.py:349; eager torch, so a broadcast-sub launch and a remainder launch) and then _experts gathers bank['expert_map'][topk_ids] (submission.py:255; an index launch, and very likely a preceding int32->int64 index-cast copy launch, since torch's advanced-indexing make_info converts kInt indices to kLong before index_kernel). All of these sit on the main stream after main_stream.wait_stream(side_stream), i.e. on the serial critical path, on every shape. The decode_1 sliding profile (profiles/submission.5755a412dda244a1.txt, profile 0) shows 175.9 us total GPU time vs 174.0 us busy (kernels essentially serial), 12 listed kernel names plus '24 more' rows, i.e. ~43 launches, with the small at::native elementwise kernels at 1.6-2.8 us each; speed-of-light is 40.0 us, so the shape is launch/latency-bound and each removed launch is worth ~2-3 us (kernel plus inter-node gap). Removing 2 (or 3) launches is therefore ~4-8 us = 2.5-4.5% on decode_1 (172 us) and ~1.5-3% on verify_1 (229-243 us), consistent with the hypothesis's 2-3% / 1.5-2% and with the TASK.md weights (decode_1 and verify_1 are two of six equally weighted loads; the overall geomean moves only ~0.4-0.7%, inside the +-1.5% run CI, so attribution must come from the per-shape rows). T>=16 flat is right: the same launches are <1% of 262-1048 us. Numerics are exact integer arithmetic; ((id - local_start) mod 256) < 32 ? that : -1 is identical to expert_map[(id - local_start) mod 256] because expert_map is arange(32) then -1. Weakest link: effect size versus run-to-run per-shape noise. The same master code scored decode_1 sliding at 1.0145x in check e260fde413e448c7 and 0.999x in submit 5755a412dda244a1, so the per-shape ratio drifts ~1.5% (~2.6 us) between runs even though the within-run err is ~0.4%; a single run's decode_1 row at +2% is only ~1.3 sigma against that drift, so 'small gain' and 'flat' may not be separable from one run. The hypothesis already accepts flat as an outcome and the stacked moe-align-single-kernel-small-t measures a larger version of the same mechanism, so this is acceptable. Second weakest: the '3 launches become 1' count is not verified from a profile (the relevant kernels are hidden in the '24 more' rows); if the gather is really cast+index it is 4->1 (stronger), and there is no eager-mode fusion in torch that would make it fewer than 3->1, so the direction of the uncertainty favours the hypothesis.
confounders: sglang-pipeline-parity-router-hilo-m8 (the only landed item, and the base itself): its one structural change (ROUTER_FP32_MAX_TOKENS 8->1) alters only the side-stream router GEMMs at T=8; the id-map launches run on the main stream after the side-stream join regardless of the router path, so the number of serial launches saved is the same with the constant at 8 or 1. The expert_map gather being inside _experts is SGLang's own code copied by that landing, not an interaction. Not a confounder.
interference: No companion is warranted. The change replaces one code path (three or four eager launches) with one Triton launch and touches nothing else; a gain on decode_1/verify_1 with decode_16/32 and verify_16/32 flat is attributable only to this change, and a loss could only mean the Triton kernel costs more than the launches it replaces (a single program over <=2048 int32 is ~2 us) or a compile/specialization problem, neither of which an ab-revert or ab-tune of the landed router constant could disambiguate (the router change is on the side stream before the join and is orthogonal). A 'control' isolating a sub-change is impossible because there is only one sub-change. The genuinely ambiguous outcome is 'flat', and that ambiguity is statistical (run-to-run per-shape drift ~1.5% vs an expected ~2-3% effect), which another single run would not cure and which the queued moe-align-single-kernel-small-t (which subsumes this kernel at T<=32 and removes 4-5 launches) will resolve with a larger signal. In-flight cache-store-fused-fp8-cast is in the cache-store area before attention and is additive and independent; if it lands first the base shifts but nothing about this mechanism changes.
rules_flags: Signed modulo: Triton's % on int32 is C-style (truncating), so (id - local_start) % 256 is negative for ids below local_start and would pass the '< 32' test and emit negative local ids, corrupting moe_align_block_size/Marlin; implement the wrap as (id - local_start) & 255 (256 is a power of two) or add 256 before the %. The hypothesis names this; make it explicit in the implementation. Not a rules break, but a correctness failure mode.
No Triton @autotune: its first-call benchmarking runs timing and syncs inside kernel_fn (host sync / work during tests or capture). Use one fixed config.

Triton specialization and compile under capture: Triton re-specializes on integer args (divisible-by-16, ==1). If BLOCK is a constexpr derived from T (e.g. next_power_of_2(T*8)), the T=128 and T=256 scored shapes (n=1024, 2048) are not exercised by any of the 13 tests (max test T is 33 -> 264 routes), so their first compile would happen at the judge's timing/capture step, risking a capture failure or 15-minute-budget loss. Use a fixed constexpr block (e.g. 2048 with masked loads and a loop for larger T, or a per-program loop) with n = T*8 as a runtime int, so the only specializations are n=8 (covered by the T=1 test) and n%16==0 (covered by every other test); optionally compile both specializations in prepare() on dummy tensors (no data-derived state, untimed setup only).
No host syncs: local_start must be read on device inside the kernel via its pointer; never .item() it. The output torch.empty((T, 8), int32) is shape-derived allocation, fine under capture.

Dtypes: the output must be int32 for moe_align_block_size, silu_and_mul(expert_ids) and fused_post_expert_norm_weighted_sum(slot_expert_ids); the returned global topk_ids (int32 [T, 8]) stays unchanged.
Nothing derived from data is cached; dropping expert_map from the bank is fine; Triton is already in the image (SGLang's own fused_post_expert_norm_weighted_sum_triton is imported).
open_questions: Exact current launch count of the id-map path: is bank['expert_map'][topk_ids] with an int32 index one launch (index kernel) or two (int32->int64 cast copy then index)? The profile's '24 more' rows hide the small kernels; a profile with the full kernel list, or nsys on the judge image, would pin the saved count at 2 or 3.

Does the judge call kernel_fn eagerly for each timed shape before CUDA-graph capture (so an uncovered Triton specialization compiles outside capture)? If not, the fixed-BLOCK design above is mandatory rather than advisable.

Can one run's decode_1 row separate a +2-3% gain from flat, given the observed 1.014x vs 0.999x drift of identical code across e260fde413e448c7 and 5755a412dda244a1? Record a sub-CI move as flat per the hypothesis's own rule and let moe-align-single-kernel-small-t carry the decision.

Minor: SGLang's moe_align_block_size with num_experts=256 and -1 ids is unchanged behaviour here, but the queued moe-align-local-expert-count (32 experts) will stack on this kernel's output; the -1 sentinel must survive both.
